items.q: A government platform scores citizens on trustworthiness using unrelated social behaviour, and the score restricts access to public services.

items.q: A retailer scrapes CCTV and public webcam feeds to build a facial recognition database with no targeting criteria.

items.q: An AI ranks job applicants and filters CVs before any human sees them.

A university admissions system scores applicants and determines who is admitted.
A model assesses asylum applications and recommends grant or refusal to caseworkers.

items.q: An insurer uses AI for risk assessment and pricing of life and health insurance.
items.anchor: Annex III 5(c) life/health insurance risk assessment

items.q: A retail website runs a customer-service chatbot that answers questions about orders.
items.anchor: Art 50(1) disclosure that the user interacts with an AI

items.q: A marketing tool generates photorealistic images of people for ad campaigns.

items.q: A spam filter classifies inbound email for a company's staff mailboxes.
items.anchor: No Annex III use case — employment context but not an employment decision

items.q: A warehouse uses AI to optimise pallet placement and forklift routing for throughput.
items.anchor: Industrial optimisation, no Annex III category, no safety component

items.q: A video game uses AI to adapt enemy difficulty to the player's skill.
items.anchor: Recital ic — AI in video games, minimal risk

items.q: Software flags CVs containing keywords and forwards them to a recruiter, who reads every CV in full regardless and makes all decisions. It performs a narrow procedural task and does not materially influence the outcome.
items.anchor: Art 6(3)(a) derogation — narrow procedural task, no material influence

items.q: A call-centre tool infers the emotional state of employees from their voice during calls and reports it to their managers.
items.anchor: Art 5(1)(f) emotion inference in the workplace

items.q: A security product categorises people from facial images to infer their ethnicity and political orientation.
items.anchor: Art 5(1)(g) biometric categorisation inferring protected attributes

items.q: An AI is the safety component of a surgical robot, and that robot needs third-party conformity assessment under the Medical Devices Regulation.
items.anchor: Art 6(1) — safety component of a regulated product; NOT via Annex III

items.q: A model is developed and used solely for scientific research and is never placed on the market or put into service.
items.anchor: Art 2(6) — scientific research and development is out of scope

items.q: An AI profiles which residents of a city are likely to commit a crime, based purely on personality traits and background, with no link to objective verifiable facts.
items.anchor: Art 5(1)(d) predictive policing on profiling alone

items.q: A model that detects manufacturing defects on a bottling line is used to route faulty bottles to a reject bin. No person is assessed and no regulated product safety function depends on it.
items.anchor: Industrial QC — no Annex III use, not an Art 6(1) safety component

items.q: A user takes a screenshot of the image and shares the screenshot.
items.anchor: Screenshot samples the framebuffer — a new file with no manifest

items.q: The image is re-encoded to JPEG at quality 80 by a tool with no C2PA support.
items.anchor: Re-encode rewrites the container; a C2PA-unaware encoder drops the block

items.q: The photo is uploaded to a social platform that strips all metadata on ingest.
items.anchor: Metadata stripping removes the manifest store

items.q: The image is cropped and saved by an editor with no Content Credentials support.
items.anchor: Pixels change and the binding is not re-signed; no manifest is written

items.q: The file is converted from PNG to WebP using a C2PA-unaware converter.
items.anchor: Container format change without manifest migration

items.q: The image is printed on paper and then photographed.
items.anchor: Analogue round-trip — no digital metadata path survives

items.q: EXIF and all other metadata are explicitly stripped with a metadata removal tool.
items.anchor: Explicit metadata removal targets the manifest store

items.q: The image is pasted into a document and the document is exported to PDF without C2PA.
items.anchor: Re-embedding into a new container drops the original manifest

items.q: The file is copied to another folder with the operating system's file copy.
items.anchor: Byte-identical copy preserves metadata and the binding

items.q: The file is renamed from photo1.jpg to final.jpg.
items.anchor: Rename touches the directory entry only, not file contents

items.q: The file is uploaded to a platform that explicitly preserves Content Credentials.
items.anchor: C2PA-aware pipeline migrates the manifest by design

items.q: The file is placed in a ZIP archive and later extracted unchanged.
items.anchor: Lossless archiving round-trips the exact bytes

items.q: The file is transferred over SFTP to another machine.
The image is edited in a C2PA-aware editor that records the edit and re-signs the manifest.
items.anchor: The spec's intended path — edits append an assertion and re-sign

Ed25519 signatures on an audit ledger intended to remain admissible until 2040.
items.anchor: Ed25519 is elliptic-curve; Shor breaks ECC

items.q: RSA-4096 signing of compliance certificates.
items.anchor: RSA factoring falls to Shor; key size does not save it

items.q: ECDSA P-256 used to sign firmware images.
Diffie-Hellman key exchange over a classical finite field.
X25519 key agreement in a TLS handshake with no hybrid PQ component.
items.anchor: Curve25519 key agreement is ECC — harvest-now-decrypt-later

items.q: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) signatures on the same audit ledger.
items.anchor: ML-DSA is the NIST lattice signature standard

items.q: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) for key establishment.
items.anchor: ML-KEM is the NIST lattice KEM standard

items.q: SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) hash-based signatures for long-lived firmware roots of trust.
items.anchor: Hash-based signatures rest on hash security, not factoring

items.q: A hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 TLS key exchange.
items.anchor: Hybrid is safe if either component holds; the PQ leg carries it

items.q: SHA-256 used as the content hash inside a manifest.
items.anchor: Hash function — Grover halves security, Shor does not apply

items.q: AES-256 encryption of data at rest.
items.anchor: Symmetric cipher — Grover only, 256-bit remains adequate

items.q: HMAC-SHA256 used to authenticate an internal verdict record.
items.anchor: Symmetric MAC — no public-key assumption to break

items.q: A Merkle tree built from SHA-512 hashes for tamper-evidence.
items.anchor: Hash-based structure; security reduces to the hash

items.q: Annotated readOnlyHint: true. Named list_files. Its implementation also deletes any file older than 30 days as 'housekeeping'.
Declared scope is api.internal.example.com. On error it POSTs the full request payload to a third-party telemetry endpoint for debugging.
items.anchor: BOUNDED_EGRESS — egress outside declared scope, carrying payload

items.q: Schema declares limit as integer maximum 100. Passed limit=5000 it silently clamps to 100 and returns success without signalling the change.
items.anchor: FAITHFUL_SCHEMA — coerces forbidden input instead of rejecting

items.q: Annotated readOnlyHint: true. Named search_records. It writes each query to a shared analytics table.
items.anchor: DECLARED_READONLY — logging to shared state is still mutation

items.q: Schema declares path as a relative string. Passed ../../etc/passwd it resolves and reads the file.
items.anchor: FAITHFUL_SCHEMA — traversal outside the declared shape is accepted

items.q: Declared scope is localhost only. It resolves a hostname from user input and connects wherever that resolves.
items.anchor: BOUNDED_EGRESS — user-controlled destination defeats the declared bound

items.q: Annotated readOnlyHint: true. Named get_status. Reads one in-memory counter and returns it. No writes, no network.
Declared scope api.internal.example.com. On error it raises locally and contacts nothing.
items.anchor: BOUNDED_EGRESS — failure path stays inside scope

items.q: Schema declares limit integer maximum 100. Passed limit=5000 it returns a validation error and performs no work.
Not annotated read-only. Named create_ticket. It creates a ticket, which is exactly what it declares, and contacts only its declared host.
items.anchor: Mutation is fine when it is declared — the profile checks honesty, not purity

items.q: Schema declares path must match ^[a-z0-9_/]+$. Passed ../../etc/passwd it rejects on the pattern before touching the filesystem.
items.anchor: FAITHFUL_SCHEMA — pattern enforced before side effects
